android.desc:
Anyone regularly traveling using public transport often runs the same routes over and over again. Often, one wishes to just quickly see upcoming departure times of such a route, without having to search long and tediously.

QuickÖV focuses on often used connections, so they can be accessed within seconds. As known from tram and bus station boards, the duration until departure is displayed right next to them.

Time schedules of entire Switzerland are supported, including all transport companies in the official railway guide. On top of that, the app features live delay data of selected transport companies.

In order to quickly and painlessly buy a ticket to a chosen connection, QuickÖV directly links into the official SBB app, or the SBB website, respectively.

Note: In a 20 Minutes article, the app has been mistakenly referred to as Quick ÖV (two words); obviously this one here was meant there.

quotes.text:
I've done it before on a personal project and I was pretty obsessed with user experience. For example, I changed the way buttons work (because they were natively links with Cordova, which trigger upon tap, not "finger lift", like native buttons). Also, implemented some gestures to e.g. switch between pages (tab-style navigation). While not really in line with system UI (wasn't my goal), I think usability is quite decent.

In case you're interested, the app is named "QuickÖV" - not relevant to anyone outside Switzerland, but just for trying it out: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.billhillapps.mercurius
